issues.detail: The Greek 'την αναστροφην υμων' (your conduct/manner of life) is rendered as 'Hãy ăn ở tốt' (Let us live well/behave well), which changes the grammatical structure from a gerundive/participial context describing a state ('having your conduct') to an imperative command ('Let us').

The Greek 'εποπτευσαντες' (having seen/observed) is rendered as 'thấy' (see), but the Vietnamese structure misses the specific nuance of 'having observed' as a completed action preceding the glorification.
